processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heating from room temperature to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature 950 °C at 5 °C/s.
Equilibrated 15 s at 950 °C so the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.
Strain rate 1 s^-1; true strain 0.92. Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
Immediately after compression the sample was water-spray quenched.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (as-forged) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries; grain interiors carry abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light striations/lamellae giving a strongly banded, dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large polygonal grains; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar (no numeric grain size printed).

structures.overall_structure: After 60% (true strain 0.92) isothermal compression at 950 °C and 1 s^-1, the DRX is partial and non-uniform. Zone 1 (difficult deformation) retains large grains, while zones 2 and 3 show banded, elongated structures of flattened original grains with numerous large elongated remnant original grains and only locally fine recrystallized grains. At low T (900-950 °C) and high strain rate (1-10 s^-1) the DRX grains are small but the DRX is not sufficient, leaving coarse original grains and poor microstructure homogeneity.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large grains (difficult deformation zone, least recrystallized).
Banded, elongated structure with numerous large elongated remnant original grains and only locally fine recrystallized grains.

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (zone 3) / core (used for grain-size measurement)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Banded, elongated structure with numerous large elongated remnant original grains and only locally fine recrystallized grains; low DRX volume fraction (partial and non-uniform).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cylindrical specimen F 8 mm × 12 mm; T = 950 °C (this sample); ε̇ = 1 s^-1; 60% compression (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant at both ends.
characterization_methods.purpose: To obtain the flow (rheological) stress curves and characterize hot deformation / dynamic recrystallization behavior.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; peak stress decreases with increasing T or decreasing ε̇.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, prepared, ground, polished and etched (30% nitric acid alcohol solution, volume fraction); 100 µm scale bars; three deformation zones imaged.
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe microstructure evolution in the three deformation zones and measure the DRX average grain size.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For this sample (950 °C, 1 s^-1), zone 1 retains large grains while zones 2 and 3 are banded/elongated with large remnant original grains and only locally fine recrystallized grains.

computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon parameter calculation (Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT)), Eq. (3), using the average DRX activation energy obtained from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine constitutive equation (Eq. (1)).

analytical_models.equation_role: Characterizes the combined effect of temperature and strain rate on flow stress and normalizes the characteristic stress-strain values.
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T; the value 65.88 corresponds to this sample's condition (950 °C, 1 s^-1) and lies between the extreme table entries (70.99 at 10 s^-1/900 °C and 52.01 at 0.01 s^-1/1150 °C).

computational_details.simulation_method: Mathematical regression (Levenberg-Marquardt optimization) of the experimental data to build the DRX average grain size prediction model; implemented as a finite element model.
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Semi-symmetric specimen; billet set as rigid-plastic body and die indenter as rigid body; shear-type contact friction = 0.3; billet-air convection coefficient = 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the isothermal compression conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted vs experimental DRX grain size: R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53%; absolute error mostly within 3 µm.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 11 generalized and Eq. 12 fitted)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts the DRX average grain size as a function of strain rate and temperature; for this sample it gives the DRX grain size at 950 °C and 1 s^-1.
analytical_models.model_note: The initial grain size and strain were treated as constants, so a·d0^h·ε^p is incorporated into the fitted constant; the model was built to predict DRX average grain size for numerical simulation of hot forging of this steel.

unmapped_findings: For the 950 °C/1 s^-1 sample, no individual numeric value is reported for peak stress, characteristic stresses/strains (σc/σp/σs, εc/εp/εs) or DRX average grain size; these are only presented within the global figures/models (Fig. 3, Fig. 6, Eq. 10, Fig. 10, Eq. 12) across all conditions.

Textual description for this condition (low T 900-950 °C together with high strain rate 1-10 s^-1): fine DRX grains tend to form but the DRX is not sufficient, and large-size original grains remain, giving poor microstructure homogeneity (Fig. 9(d)).

The DRX average grain size of this sample is only shown graphically in Fig. 10 (curve for ε̇ = 1 s^-1 at 950 °C); no numeric readout is printed, and it lies above the 900 °C values (which are between ~0 and 20 µm) and below the 1150 °C/0.01 s^-1 value that exceeds 70 µm.
The etching solution used to reveal the microstructure before laser-confocal imaging was a 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction).
